title: Paraprofessional
subtitle: Classified
salaryRange: Compensation and work schedules are structured in accordance with current District policy.
roleDescription: The Paraprofessional supports student success by providing instructional reinforcement under the direction of classroom teachers, attending to students' physical, personal, academic, and behavioral needs, and serving as a positive, nurturing guide across instructional and non-instructional settings.
roleHighlight: Core Support Role: This position serves as an essential instructional partner, modeling the district's professional, ethical, and communication standards while fostering collaborative relationships with students, staff, and families.
responsibilities: Provide instructional reinforcement of lesson plans under the direct guidance of special education and classroom teachers
Serve as a positive, nurturing guide and role model for students across all school environments
Supervise students in both instructional and non-instructional settings to maintain a safe learning environment
Support student learning of lesson components through classwork review, guided discussion, and direct assistance
Attend to students' physical, personal, academic, and behavioral/emotional needs as required throughout the school day
Perform essential classroom preparation duties, including organizing and preparing specialized teaching materials
Model high professional, ethical, and communication standards when interacting with students, staff, and community members
Establish and maintain cooperative, supportive working relationships with students, parents, and building staff
Performs other related duties, training, and responsibilities as assigned to ensure effective classroom operations
requiredQuals: Secure appropriate Illinois State Board of Education Paraprofessional Certification (or eligible credential)
High school diploma or general education degree (GED) equivalent at minimum
Effective oral and written communication skills with both adults and school-age children
preferredQuals: Prior experience working successfully with school-age children in an educational or child-care setting
Demonstrated ability to adapt to diverse student needs and support behavioral/emotional interventions
Strong interpersonal skills with a collaborative, team-oriented approach to classroom support
Basic proficiency with classroom technology and learning management tools
benefits: Competitive District-Subsidized Medical, Dental, and Life Insurance Plans
Illinois Municipal Retirement Fund (IMRF) Pension Participation Framework
Optional Employee Contribution Access to 403(b) and 457 Retirement Accounts
Fixed Annual Allotments of Sick and Personal Leave Days
cultureText: Paraprofessionals operate within a highly collaborative classroom environment dedicated to individual student growth. Physical demands include regularly sitting, standing, walking, traversing stairs, operating school equipment, reaching, and occasionally lifting or moving up to 20 pounds.
matchQuestions: Do you hold (or are you eligible for) an ISBE Paraprofessional Certification?
Do you have experience supporting the academic, behavioral, or physical needs of school-age children?
Are you comfortable supervising students in both classroom and non-instructional settings (e.g., recess, lunch, hallways)?
Can you work collaboratively under the direction of classroom teachers while maintaining professional boundaries?
